findings.evidence: R9 and AC33 explicitly permit configured external URLs as escaped data while prohibiting their use in resource-loading or navigation positions.
AC35 verifies provenance for overlay values, environment references, explicit base values equal to defaults, unset defaults, and removal of an override.
A5, AC29 and AC34 specify the watched status path, external-process publication setup, discovery tests and operator documentation.
A8, R1 and AC36 define wildcard-bind authorities, allowed host names, IPv6 brackets, case matching and browser Origin syntax.

new_findings.title: Editing scope contradicts the binding brief
new_findings.evidence: A2 and R6 make triggers, actions, limits and modules_directory read-only, whereas binding decision 6b in the brief requires writing everything except secrets; AC25 enforces this reduced scope. The specification is not sound enough to plan from until this contradiction is resolved.

new_findings.title: Status transition publication lacks acceptance coverage
new_findings.evidence: R7 requires atomic status publication on becoming ready and on every module ready/degraded transition, but AC31 checks only record creation, contents and the environment-variable opt-out; AC18 and AC29 consume supplied records. No acceptance criterion verifies transition-triggered publication or atomic replacement of the status record.
